classification.difficultyReason: The student must select and link the three taught coefficient relations, recognise that the pair sum is αβ+(α+β)², and eliminate α+β and αβ to obtain a linear equation for k. The root representation is supplied and the same elimination pattern appears in the source; no additional insight or individual-root solving is required.

content.prompt: The cubic equation $x^3-8x^2+kx+2k+4=0$ has roots $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\alpha+\beta$. Show that $k=10$.

answer.worked:
Sum of roots:
$$2\alpha+2\beta=8\qquad(1)$$
Sum of products of pairs of roots:
$$\alpha\beta+\beta(\alpha+\beta)+\alpha(\alpha+\beta)=k\qquad(2)$$
Product of roots:
$$\alpha\beta(\alpha+\beta)=-(2k+4)\qquad(3)$$
Rearranging (1) gives $\alpha+\beta=4$. Substituting into (2),
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha\beta+4\beta+4\alpha&=k\\\alpha\beta+4(\alpha+\beta)&=k\\\alpha\beta+16&=k\\\alpha\beta&=k-16.\end{aligned}$$
Substituting $\alpha+\beta$ and $\alpha\beta$ into (3),
$$\begin{aligned}4(k-16)&=-(2k+4)\\4k-64&=-2k-4\\6k&=60\\k&=10.\end{aligned}$$
